novelty.justification: The claim proposes a new phenomenon/mechanistic relationship: “the channel is signed and bidirectional,” such that data from a teacher whose trait is “actively SUPPRESSED” causes a student that already has the trait to move away from it, yielding content-free “subliminal unlearning.” Searches for “subliminal learning negative steering vector unlearning,” “signed bidirectional trait transmission hidden signals,” and “steering vector distillation suppressed teacher” identified Cloud et al., “Subliminal Learning: Language models transmit behavioral traits via hidden signals in data” (2025; Nature version 2026), and “Subliminal Learning Is Steering Vector Distillation” (2026) as the closest work; the latter already distills semantic and random steering vectors and explains transfer through activation-gradient alignment, while existing unlearning work such as “Unlearning Isn’t Deletion” studies suppression versus genuine erasure but not transmission through trait-free teacher outputs. Moving from arbitrary steering-vector distillation to deliberately negative trait directions is a natural but non-trivial extension, and combining it with the requirement that a pre-equipped student lose the trait changes the direction and interpretation of transmission; however, the signed prediction is already strongly implied by the closest mechanism rather than requiring an entirely new core principle, so this is standard-to-moderately-strong novelty rather than a 7–8 breakthrough.
